newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics up on Hitachi deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics up on Hitachi deal.

text.p: Shares of U.S. Robotics Corp rose 3-1/4 to 77 Wednesday after Hitachi PC Corp said it would use the modem maker's high-speed "x2" technology in its notebook computers.

"Hitachi has just gotten into the notebook business, but they've got good machines that are very aggressively priced," said Amar Senan, an analyst with Volpe, Welty & Co. "It's nothing earth-shattering but the bulls love it."
Hitachi PC is a unit of Tokyo-based Hitachi Ltd.
Analysts also said a decline in U.S. Robotics on Tuesday, after an analyst cautioned about a possible weak December quarter, was overdone, providing a solid buying opportunity today.
"Basically, we think even if there is a blooper this quarter it wouldn't scare us off unless it is very significant," said Bear Sterns analyst Eric Blachno.
He reiterated his buy rating on U.S. Robotics.
The current fiscal first quarter is a transition for U.S. Robotics as it prepares to launch its "x2" modem products.
"We think (accelerated growth) is going to come in the June quarter," with x2 product sales in full swing, Blachno said.

U.S. Robotics's x2 technology will allow users to download information from the Internet at 56 kilobits per second over conventional telephone lines -- almost twice as fast as today's common 28.8 kbps modems.
